# Sloc Cloc and Code (scc)

![SCC illustration](./scc.jpg)

A tool similar to cloc, sloccount and tokei. For counting the lines of code, blank lines, comment lines, and physical lines of source code in many programming languages.

Goal is to be the fastest code counter possible, but also perform COCOMO calculation like sloccount, LOCOMO estimation for LLM-based development costs, estimate code complexity similar to cyclomatic complexity calculators and produce unique lines of code or DRYness metrics. In short one tool to rule them all.

Also it has a very short name which is easy to type `scc`.

If you don't like sloc cloc and code feel free to use the name `Succinct Code Counter`.

Licensed under MIT licence.

## Install

### Snap

A snap install exists.

`$ sudo snap install scc`

*NB* Snap installed applications cannot run outside of `/home` so you may encounter issues if you use snap and attempt to run outside this directory.

### Homebrew

Or if you have Homebrew installed

`$ brew install scc`

### Fedora

Fedora Linux users can use a COPR repository:

`$ sudo dnf copr enable lihaohong/scc && sudo dnf install scc`

### MacPorts

On macOS, you can also install via MacPorts

`$ sudo port install scc`

### Scoop

Or if you are using Scoop on Windows

`$ scoop install scc`

### Chocolatey

Or if you are using Chocolatey on Windows

`$ choco install scc`

### WinGet

Or if you are using WinGet on Windows

`winget install --id benboyter.scc --source winget`

### FreeBSD

On FreeBSD, scc is available as a package

`$ pkg install scc`

Or, if you prefer to build from source, you can use the ports tree

`$ cd /usr/ports/devel/scc && make install clean`

### Run in Docker

Go to the directory you want to run scc from.

Run the command below to run the latest release of scc on your current working directory:

```bash
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/pwd"  ghcr.io/boyter/scc:master scc /pwd
```

### Manual

Binaries for Windows, GNU/Linux and macOS for both i386 and x86_64 machines are available from the releases page.

## Usage

Command line usage of `scc` is designed to be as simple as possible.
Full details can be found in `scc --help` or `scc -h`.

```text

Usage:
  scc [flags] [files or directories]

Flags:
      --avg-wage int                       average wage value used for basic COCOMO calculation (default 56286)
      --binary                             disable binary file detection
      --by-file                            display output for every file
  -m, --character                          calculate max and mean characters per line
      --ci                                 enable CI output settings where stdout is ASCII
      --cocomo-project-type string         change COCOMO model type [organic, semi-detached, embedded, "custom,1,1,1,1"] (default "organic")
      --count-as string                    count extension as language [e.g. jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" maps extension jsp to html and chead to C Header]
      --count-ignore                       set to allow .gitignore and .ignore files to be counted
      --currency-symbol string             set currency symbol (default "$")
      --debug                              enable debug output
      --directory-walker-job-workers int   controls the maximum number of workers which will walk the directory tree (default 8)

## Unique Lines of Code (ULOC)

ULOC can be used to determine how many DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) code you have. It provides a measurement of unique lines of code.

To get ULOC output use the `--uloc` flag or `-u`:

```text
$ scc --uloc .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    ULOC
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076   4,456
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

To calculate DRYness percentage use the `--dryness` flag or `-a`:

```text
$ scc --dryness .
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    DRYness
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076       74.4%
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

## COCOMO

COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) calculates the estimated cost to build the code. scc uses the basic COCOMO model to provide estimates.

The COCOMO calculation is always run and will appear at the bottom of the output unless you use `--no-cocomo`.

Example:

```text
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Estimated Cost to Develop (organic) $12,517,562
Estimated Schedule Effort (organic) 35.93 months
Estimated People Required (organic) 30.95
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

You can customize COCOMO calculation with:

- `--avg-wage` - Set the average wage (default 56286)
- `--cocomo-project-type` - Change COCOMO model type: organic, semi-detached, embedded (default "organic")
- `--eaf` - Effort adjustment factor (default 1.0)
- `--currency-symbol` - Set currency symbol (default "$")

## LOCOMO

LOCOMO is an extension of COCOMO for calculating costs when using LLM (Large Language Model) based development approaches. It estimates token counts, API costs, and developer time when using AI assistants.

This is an experimental feature for estimating costs when using AI-powered development tools.

## Output Formats

scc supports multiple output formats for integration with other tools:

- `tabular` (default) - Human-readable table format
- `wide` - Wider table with additional statistics
- `json` - JSON format for programmatic processing
- `json2` - Alternative JSON format
- `csv` - CSV format
- `csv-stream` - Streaming CSV format
- `cloc-yaml` - YAML format compatible with cloc
- `html` - HTML report
- `html-table` - HTML table only
- `sql` - SQL CREATE and INSERT statements
- `sql-insert` - SQL INSERT statements only
- `openmetrics` - OpenMetrics/Prometheus format

Example:

```bash
scc --format json .
scc --format csv --output report.csv .
```

## Ignore Files

`scc` supports .ignore files inside directories that it scans. This is similar to how ripgrep, ag and tokei work. .ignore files are 100% the same as .gitignore files with the same syntax, and as such `scc` will ignore files and directories listed in them. You can add .ignore files to ignore things like vendored dependency checked in files.

By default scc will also respect .gitignore files.

## Large File Detection

scc can identify and optionally exclude large files from counting to focus on code that matters.

Use `--large-line-count` and `--large-byte-count` to set thresholds, and `--no-large` to exclude them from output.

## Minified/Generated File Detection

scc can identify minified and generated files and optionally exclude them from counts.

- `--min` - Identify minified files
- `--gen` - Identify generated files
- `--no-min` - Exclude minified files from output
- `--no-gen` - Exclude generated files from output
- `--no-min-gen` - Exclude both minified and generated files

## Remapping

You can remap file extensions to different languages using the `--count-as` flag:

```bash
scc --count-as jsp:htm,chead:"C Header" .
```

This maps `.jsp` files to HTML and `.chead` files to C Header.

You can also remap based on file content:

- `--remap-unknown` - Check unknown file types for a string and remap
- `--remap-all` - Check all files for a string and remap

Example:

```bash
scc --remap-unknown "-*- C++ -*-":"C Header" .
```

## Badges

You can generate badges for your repository showing lines of code counts.

The service at `https://sloc.xyz/` provides badges for GitHub repositories.

Note that you don't have to specify the directory you want to run against. Running `scc` will assume you want to run against the current directory.

You can also run against multiple files or directories `scc directory1 directory2 file1 file2` with the results aggregated in the output.

## Features

`scc` includes many features to help you count code accurately:

- Very fast and gets faster the more CPU you throw at it
- Accurate
- Works very well across multiple platforms without slowdown (Windows, Linux, macOS)
- Large language support
- Can ignore duplicate files
- Has complexity estimations
- You need to tell the difference between Coq and Verilog in the same directory
- cloc yaml output support so potentially a drop in replacement for some users
- Can identify or ignore minified files
- Able to identify many #! files
- Can ignore large files by lines or bytes
- Can calculate the ULOC or unique lines of code by file, language or project
- Supports multiple output formats for integration, CSV, SQL, JSON, HTML and more

## Complexity Estimates

Complexity estimates are provided for supported languages. The complexity estimate is an approximation similar to cyclomatic complexity. The intent is not to be perfect but provide a good enough indic

Example output with complexity enabled:

```text
$ scc --complexity
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────�
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────�
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076
```

## Unique Lines of Code (ULOC)

ULOC can be used to determine how many DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) code you have. It provides a measurement of unique lines of code.

To get ULOC output use the `--uloc` flag or `-u`:

```text
$ scc --uloc .
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────�
Language                 Files     Lines   Blanks  Comments     Code Complexity    ULOC
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────�
Go                          13     7,340      896       455    5,989      1,076   4,456
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────�
```

actions.command:
cd /tmp/probe && python3 - <<'EOF'
import json, collections
d = json.load(open('quotes_stage3.json'))
cnt = collections.Counter()
for lang, v in d.items():
    if v.get('quotes') is None: continue
    for o, c, e in v['quotes']:
        cnt[(o, c, str(e))] += 1
for k, n in sorted(cnt.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
    print(n, k)
EOF

def run_batch(ext, contents, target):

    return res
def minimize(ext, target, prefix, tokens):
    """prefix: content providing base keywords. tokens: list of known-matching tokens. Greedy shrink."""
    result = {}
    cur = {t: t for t in tokens}
    while True:
        cands = {}
        for t, c in cur.items():
            if len(c) <= 1: continue
            cands[t + '|L'] = c[1:]
            cands[t + '|R'] = c[:-1]
        if not cands: break
        res = run_batch(ext, {k: prefix + v + '\n' for k, v in cands.items()}, target)
        changed = False
        for t in list(cur):
            c = cur[t]
            if res.get(t + '|L'): cur[t] = c[1:]; changed = True
            elif res.get(t + '|R'): cur[t] = c[:-1]; changed = True
        if not changed: break
    return cur

	fs.Bool(&opts.NoLarge, "no-large", "", false, "ignore files over certain byte and line size set by large-line-count and large-byte-count")
	fs.Bool(&opts.NoMin, "no-min", "", false, "ignore minified files in output (implies --min)")
	fs.Bool(&opts.NoMinGen, "no-min-gen", "", false, "ignore minified or generated files in output (implies --min-gen)")
	fs.Bool(&opts.NoSccIgnore, "no-scc-ignore", "", false, "disables .sccignore file logic")
	fs.Bool(&opts.NoSize, "no-size", "", false, "remove size calculation output")

	fs.String(&opts.Output, "output", "o", "", "output filename (default stdout)")
	fs.Float(&opts.Overhead, "overhead", "", 2.4, "set the overhead multiplier for corporate overhead (facilities, equipment, accounting, etc.)")
	fs.Bool(&opts.Percent, "percent", "p", false, "include percentage values in output")
	fs.String(&opts.RemapAll, "remap-all", "", "", "inspect every file and remap by checking for a string and remapping the language [e.g. \"-*- C++ -*-\":\"C Header\"]")
	fs.String(&opts.RemapUnknown, "remap-unknown", "", "", "inspect files of unknown type and remap by checking for a string and remapping the language [e.g. \"-*- C++ -*-\":\"C Header\"]")
	fs.String(&opts.SizeUnit, "size-unit", "", "si", "set size unit [si, binary, mixed, xkcd-kb, xkcd-kelly, xkcd-imaginary, xkcd-intel, xkcd-drive, xkcd-bakers]")
	fs.Bool(&opts.SloccountFormat, "sloccount-format", "", false, "print a more SLOCCount like COCOMO calculation")
	fs.String(&opts.Sort, "sort", "s", "files", "column to sort by [files, name, lines, blanks, code, comments, complexity]")
	fs.String(&opts.SQLProject, "sql-project", "", "", "use supplied name as the project identifier for the current run. Only valid with the --format sql or sql-insert option")
	fs.Bool(&opts.Trace, "trace", "t", false, "enable trace output (not recommended when processing multiple files)")
	fs.Bool(&opts.Uloc, "uloc", "u", false, "calculate the number of unique lines of code (ULOC) for the project")
	fs.Bool(&opts.Verbose, "verbose", "v", false, "verbose output")
	fs.Bool(&opts.VersionFlag, "version", "", false, "version for scc")
	fs.Bool(&opts.Wide, "wide", "w", false, "wider output with additional statistics (implies --complexity)")
	return fs
}

func usageText(fs *flagSet) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString("Usage:\n  scc [flags] [files or directories]\n\nFlags:\n")
	sb.WriteString(fs.Usage())
	return sb.String()
}

func helpText(fs *flagSet) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString("Sloc, Cloc and Code. Count lines of code in a directory with complexity estimation.\nVersion " + Version + "\nBen Boyter <ben@boyter.org> + Contributors\n\n")
	sb.WriteString(usageText(fs))
	return sb.String()
}

func main() {
	loadLanguages()
	fs := buildFlagSet()
	if err := fs.Parse(os.Args[1:]); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "Error: "+err.Error())
		fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, usageText(fs))
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if opts.Help {
		fmt.Print(helpText(fs))
		return
	}
	if opts.VersionFlag {
		fmt.Println("scc version " + Version)
		return
	}
	if opts.MCP {
		runMCP()
		return
	}
	if opts.Languages {
		printLanguages()
		return
	}
	run(fs.args)
}

func printLanguages() {
	var sb strings.Builder
	for _, d := range LanguageDefs {
		sb.WriteString(d.Name + " (" + strings.Join(d.ListExtensions, ",") + ")\n")
	}
	fmt.Print(sb.String())
}

func usageText(fs *flagSet) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString("Usage:\n  scc [flags] [files or directories]\n\nFlags:\n")
	sb.WriteString(fs.Usage())
	return sb.String()
}

func helpText(fs *flagSet) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString("Sloc, Cloc and Code. Count lines of code in a directory with complexity estimation.\nVersion " + Version + "\nBen Boyter <ben@boyter.org> + Contributors\n\n")
	sb.WriteString(usageText(fs))
	return sb.String()
}

func main() {
	loadLanguages()
	fs := buildFlagSet()
	if err := fs.Parse(os.Args[1:]); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "Error: "+err.Error())
		fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, usageText(fs))
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if opts.Help {
		fmt.Print(helpText(fs))
		return
	}
	if opts.VersionFlag {
		fmt.Println("scc version " + Version)
		return
	}
	if opts.MCP {
		runMCP()
		return
	}
	if opts.Languages {
		printLanguages()
		return
	}
	run(fs.args)
}

func printLanguages() {
	var sb strings.Builder
	for _, d := range LanguageDefs {
		sb.WriteString(d.Name + " (" + strings.Join(d.ListExtensions, ",") + ")\n")
	}
	fmt.Print(sb.String())
}

{"command":"cd /workspace && cat > NOTES.md <<'EOF'
# Implementation notes

This repository contains an original, from-scratch reimplementation of the `scc`
command line tool (version 3.7.0 behaviour), written in Go with no third party
dependencies.

Layout:

- `main.go` – entry point and command line definition.
- `flags.go` – a small pflag/cobra compatible argument parser (help text,
  error messages, `--flag=value`, combined short flags, string slices ...).
- `languages.json` / `languages.go` – language database (extensions, filenames,
  comment and string delimiters, complexity tokens, shebang names and keyword
  lists used to disambiguate shared extensions) and the detection logic.
- `process.go` – the line counting state machine (blank / code / comment /
  multi line comment / string / docstring), binary detection, minified and
  generated detection, ULOC and line length statistics.
- `walker.go` / `gitignore.go` – directory traversal honouring `.gitignore`,
  `.ignore`, `.sccignore` and `.gitmodules` as well as the exclude options.
- `scc.go` – orchestration: option handling, concurrent processing,
  aggregation and sorting.
- `formatters.go` – tabular, wide, json, json2, csv, csv-stream, cloc-yaml,
  html, html-table, sql, sql-insert and openmetrics output.
- `cocomo.go` / `locomo.go` – cost estimation models.
- `mcp.go` – a minimal JSON-RPC (Model Context Protocol) server over stdio.

Build with `./compile.sh` which produces `./executable`.
EOF
